title: Cambridge FCE B2 First
content_provenance: Original practice items authored from the public Cambridge B2 First syllabus. Not a capture of past exam questions.

items.stem: A passage describes a repair cafe where volunteers mend broken household items for free and notes that the scheme cuts waste while teaching practical skills. What is the writer's main point about the cafe?
options: It reduces waste and shares practical skills at the same time.
It exists mainly to make a profit for its organisers.
It is a government programme for unemployed workers.
It sells new goods at lower prices than shops.
items.explanation: The passage ties the cafe to cutting waste and teaching skills, so the main point combines an environmental benefit with learning, not profit or sales.
items.reference: Cambridge B2 First Syllabus - Reading and Use of English

items.stem: A text explains that the town's new library opens on Saturdays until eight in the evening and offers free Wi-Fi throughout the building. Which detail about the library does the text give?
options: It opens on Saturdays until eight and has free Wi-Fi.
It charges visitors for Wi-Fi access.
It opens only in the mornings.
items.explanation: The text states the Saturday closing time of eight and free Wi-Fi, so the other options contradict the stated opening hours and the no-cost Wi-Fi.
items.reference: Cambridge B2 First Syllabus - Reading and Use of English

items.stem: A travel article says the mountain path is well marked but warns that sudden fog can hide the signs within minutes. What can be inferred about the path?
options: It is closed to walkers during the summer.
Its direction signs have been removed.
It can become difficult to follow when fog arrives.
It is suitable only for expert climbers.
items.explanation: If fog can hide well-placed signs within minutes, the route can quickly become hard to follow, which the other options do not support.
items.reference: Cambridge B2 First Syllabus - Reading and Use of English

items.stem: A review notes that the film's ending was abrupt and left the audience puzzled. In this context, what does abrupt most nearly mean?
items.explanation: An ending that puzzles the audience because it comes abruptly is sudden and unexpected, while the other choices describe the opposite qualities.
items.reference: Cambridge B2 First Syllabus - Reading and Use of English

items.stem: A paragraph describes how Maya trained for months and then, despite her nerves, finished the race, adding that this surprised everyone who knew her. What does the word this refer to?
options: Finishing the race despite her nerves
items.explanation: The pronoun this points back to the whole achievement of finishing the race despite nerves, which is what surprised her acquaintances.
items.reference: Cambridge B2 First Syllabus - Reading and Use of English

items.stem: A blogger writes a post listing five free apps for learning vocabulary and includes step-by-step screenshots for each. What is the main purpose of the post?
options: To criticise the apps as useless
To help readers start using the apps
To sell a paid language course
items.explanation: Listing free apps with step-by-step screenshots is intended to help readers begin using them, not to criticise, sell a course or compare phones.
items.reference: Cambridge B2 First Syllabus - Reading and Use of English

items.stem: A paragraph says a bakery's profits rose sharply in its third year, and the next sentence begins with a linking phrase meaning as a result. Which sentence would best follow?
options: As a result, the owner decided to close the bakery.
As a result, sales fell to zero within weeks.
As a result, the owner was able to open a second shop.
As a result, all the recipes were forgotten.
items.explanation: A result clause should follow logically from rising profits, so opening a second shop fits, while closing down or losing all sales contradicts the cause.
items.reference: Cambridge B2 First Syllabus - Reading and Use of English

items.stem: Complete the sentence with the correct form of the word in capitals. Her blank of the problem impressed the whole team. (ANALYSE)
items.explanation: The sentence needs a noun after the possessive her, and analysis is the noun form, while analyse is a verb and analytical and analysed are other forms.
items.reference: Cambridge B2 First Syllabus - Reading and Use of English

items.stem: Choose the word that correctly completes the sentence. The team carried out a detailed blank into the causes of the delay.
items.explanation: After the article a detailed the sentence requires a noun, so investigation fits, while investigate is a verb and the other forms are adjectives or verbs.
items.reference: Cambridge B2 First Syllabus - Reading and Use of English

items.stem: Choose the word that best completes the sentence. She has lived in Rome blank 2018 and still loves the city.
items.explanation: With a present perfect and a specific starting point, the correct preposition is since, while for is used with a length of time and from and during do not fit here.
items.reference: Cambridge B2 First Syllabus - Reading and Use of English

items.stem: Choose the best word to complete the sentence. The manager was very blank with the results and thanked the whole team.
items.explanation: The phrase be pleased with describes a person's satisfaction, whereas please is a verb, pleasing describes something, and pleasure is a noun.
items.reference: Cambridge B2 First Syllabus - Reading and Use of English

items.stem: A text says the negotiator played her cards close to her chest. What does this phrase most likely mean?
options: She was openly confident about her plans.
She gave up the discussion very quickly.
She revealed everything to the other side.
She kept her plans and intentions secret.
items.explanation: To play your cards close to your chest means to hide your intentions, so secrecy is the meaning, not openness or surrender.
items.reference: Cambridge B2 First Syllabus - Reading and Use of English

items.stem: A writer describes a new museum as impressive in scale, though disappointingly thin on real content. What is the writer's attitude towards the museum?
options: Admiration for its size mixed with criticism of its content
Total rejection of everything about it
items.explanation: Praising the scale while calling the content thin mixes approval with criticism, which is neither uncritical praise nor total rejection.
items.reference: Cambridge B2 First Syllabus - Reading and Use of English

items.stem: A paragraph explains that despite rising prices, demand for electric bicycles has kept growing, driven by cheaper running costs. What is the paragraph mainly about?
options: The falling price of petrol worldwide
The reasons demand for electric bicycles keeps rising
How to repair an old bicycle at home
Why electric bicycles are becoming cheaper
items.explanation: The paragraph stresses that demand keeps growing and explains why through running costs, so its main topic is the reasons behind that demand.
items.reference: Cambridge B2 First Syllabus - Reading and Use of English

items.stem: A passage describes the expedition as arduous and later calls the same route demanding. What is the relationship between the two words?
options: One of them is a number.
items.explanation: Both arduous and demanding describe something that requires great effort, so the words are close in meaning rather than opposites or unrelated.
items.reference: Cambridge B2 First Syllabus - Reading and Use of English

items.stem: A text says the council approved the plan but the mayor opposed it. What does the pronoun it refer to in the sentence?
items.explanation: The pronoun it stands in for the plan, which is the thing the mayor opposed, not the mayor, the council or the text.
items.reference: Cambridge B2 First Syllabus - Reading and Use of English

items.stem: A writer first presents the benefits of remote work, then lists its drawbacks, and ends by suggesting a balanced approach. How is the text organised?
options: Advantages, then disadvantages, then a balanced view
A single list of unrelated facts
A story with characters and dialogue
items.explanation: The order of benefits, then drawbacks, then a balanced suggestion gives a three-part structure, not a one-sided list or a story.
items.reference: Cambridge B2 First Syllabus - Reading and Use of English

items.stem: A long article about plastic recycling explains collection, sorting and the limits of current technology. Which sentence best summarises the article?
options: Recycling plastic is a flawless process.
Recycling plastic is useful but limited by technology.
Plastic should never be recycled at all.
items.explanation: A summary must capture both the usefulness and the technological limits, so the balanced sentence is best, while the others overstate or misread the article.
items.reference: Cambridge B2 First Syllabus - Reading and Use of English

items.stem: Text A argues that school trips build confidence, while Text B argues that they are too expensive to justify. What do the two texts disagree about?
options: The length of the school day
The price of local bus tickets
Whether school trips are worth their cost
items.explanation: One text defends the value of trips while the other stresses their cost, so the disagreement is whether they are worth the expense.
items.reference: Cambridge B2 First Syllabus - Reading and Use of English

items.stem: A columnist writes that city centre car bans are unpopular but unavoidable. What does the columnist believe about the bans?
options: They are widely popular with drivers.
They cost the city nothing at all.
They are necessary even though many people oppose them.
items.explanation: Calling the bans unavoidable while admitting they are unpopular means the columnist thinks they are necessary despite public opposition.
items.reference: Cambridge B2 First Syllabus - Reading and Use of English

items.stem: You hear a student explaining why she missed the lecture. She says her bus broke down and she had to walk the rest of the way. Why did she miss the lecture?
options: Her bus broke down on the way.
items.explanation: The student gives the broken bus and the walk as the reason, so the other explanations are not mentioned in what she says.
items.reference: Cambridge B2 First Syllabus - Listening

items.stem: You hear a man booking a hotel room. He asks for a quiet room on a high floor away from the lifts. What does he request?
options: A quiet room on a high floor
A room with a sea view
A smoking room on the ground floor
items.explanation: The man specifies a quiet room on a high floor and away from the lifts, so the other room descriptions do not match his request.
items.reference: Cambridge B2 First Syllabus - Listening

items.stem: You hear two friends discussing a film. One says the acting was excellent but the plot was weak. What is her opinion of the film?
options: The film is excellent in every way.
The film is completely boring from start to finish.
The acting is good but the plot is poor.
The film is far too short.
items.explanation: Her comment praises the acting while criticising the plot, giving a mixed view rather than uniform praise, boredom or a comment on length.
items.reference: Cambridge B2 First Syllabus - Listening

items.stem: You hear a weather report saying heavy rain will stop by midday and the afternoon will be sunny and warm. What will the afternoon be like?
items.explanation: The report says the afternoon will be sunny and warm once the rain stops, so the rainy, snowy and foggy options contradict the forecast.
items.reference: Cambridge B2 First Syllabus - Listening

items.stem: You hear a guide explaining that the walking tour lasts two hours and finishes at the castle gates. How long does the tour last?
items.explanation: The guide states the tour lasts two hours, so the other durations are not what is given in the announcement.
items.reference: Cambridge B2 First Syllabus - Listening

items.stem: You hear a woman complaining that her train was delayed by forty minutes because of signal problems. What was the length of the delay?
items.explanation: She gives the delay as forty minutes, so the smaller figures and the one-hour option misreport the length she states.
items.reference: Cambridge B2 First Syllabus - Listening

items.stem: You hear a teacher tell the class that the deadline has moved from Friday to Monday. What is the new deadline?
items.explanation: The teacher changes the deadline to Monday, so Friday is the old date and Wednesday and Sunday are never mentioned.
items.reference: Cambridge B2 First Syllabus - Listening

items.stem: You hear a shop assistant say the item is out of stock but can be ordered for delivery next week. What does the assistant offer to do?
options: Give the customer a full refund
Find a different colour in stock
Order the item for delivery next week
items.explanation: The assistant offers to order the item for delivery next week, and no refund, alternative colour or discount is mentioned.
items.reference: Cambridge B2 First Syllabus - Listening

items.stem: You hear a man say he prefers cycling to work because it keeps him fit and saves money on fares. Why does he cycle to work?
options: It keeps him fit and saves money.
He has no other way to travel.
The bus is faster than cycling.
He dislikes walking in the morning.
items.explanation: The man gives fitness and saved fares as his reasons, so the other options are not the reasons he states.
items.reference: Cambridge B2 First Syllabus - Listening

items.stem: You hear an announcement that the museum is closing in fifteen minutes and visitors should leave through the main entrance. Where should visitors leave?
items.explanation: The announcement directs visitors to the main entrance, so the side door, roof and car park are not the exit named.
items.reference: Cambridge B2 First Syllabus - Listening

items.stem: You hear a woman inviting a friend to dinner on Saturday and asking her to bring a dessert. What does she ask her friend to bring?
items.explanation: The invitation asks the friend to bring a dessert, so a main course, a drink or nothing do not match the request.
items.reference: Cambridge B2 First Syllabus - Listening

items.stem: You hear a podcast host say the guest grew up in a small village and later moved to the city. Where did the guest grow up?
items.explanation: The host says the guest grew up in a small village, so the city is where the guest moved later and the other options are not stated.
items.reference: Cambridge B2 First Syllabus - Listening

items.stem: You hear a doctor advise a patient to rest for three days and drink plenty of water. What two pieces of advice does the doctor give?
options: Rest and drink plenty of water
items.explanation: The doctor recommends rest and plenty of water, so exercise, travel and extra work are the opposite of the advice given.
items.reference: Cambridge B2 First Syllabus - Listening

items.stem: You hear a man say the concert was cancelled because the singer lost her voice. Why was the concert cancelled?
options: The venue was closed for repairs.
items.explanation: The man gives the singer's lost voice as the cause, so sold-out tickets, a closed venue and flooding are not the stated reasons.
items.reference: Cambridge B2 First Syllabus - Listening

items.stem: You hear a receptionist say the meeting room is on the second floor, directly opposite the stairs. Where is the meeting room?
options: In the basement by the car park
On the ground floor near the entrance
On the second floor opposite the stairs
items.explanation: The receptionist places the room on the second floor opposite the stairs, so the basement, ground floor and outside options are wrong.
items.reference: Cambridge B2 First Syllabus - Listening

items.stem: You hear a woman say she has taken up photography and now spends her weekends taking pictures of birds. What is her new hobby?
items.explanation: She says she has taken up photography and photographs birds at weekends, so the other activities are not her new hobby.
items.reference: Cambridge B2 First Syllabus - Listening

items.stem: You hear a traffic report warning of long delays on the motorway because of an accident near junction five. What has caused the delays?
items.explanation: The report names an accident near junction five as the cause, so road works, weather and a match are not what caused the delays.
items.reference: Cambridge B2 First Syllabus - Listening

items.stem: You hear a man say he will pay by card because he has no cash with him today. How will he pay?
options: He will not pay at all
items.explanation: The man says he will pay by card since he has no cash, so cash, cheque and not paying do not reflect what he says.
items.reference: Cambridge B2 First Syllabus - Listening

items.stem: You hear two colleagues agree to meet at the cafe at half past two tomorrow afternoon. What time will they meet?
items.explanation: The colleagues agree on half past two, so the other times are near-misses that were not the time arranged.
items.reference: Cambridge B2 First Syllabus - Listening

items.stem: You hear a mother remind her son to take an umbrella because it may rain later in the day. Why should the son take an umbrella?
options: The sun will be very strong.
items.explanation: The mother's reason is the chance of rain later, so strong sun, snow and swimming are not the reason she gives.
items.reference: Cambridge B2 First Syllabus - Listening

items.stem: Choose the correct preposition to complete the sentence. She is very good blank solving difficult problems under pressure.
items.explanation: The adjective good is followed by at before a gerund describing an activity, while in, on and for do not form this fixed pattern.
items.reference: Cambridge B2 First Syllabus - Vocabulary and Grammar

items.stem: Choose the best phrasal verb. The meeting was blank until next week because the manager was ill.
items.explanation: To put off a meeting means to postpone it, which matches the reason given, whereas put up, put on and put out have unrelated meanings.
items.reference: Cambridge B2 First Syllabus - Vocabulary and Grammar

items.stem: Choose the correct verb form. By the time we arrived at the cinema, the film blank.
items.explanation: An action completed before another past action takes the past perfect, so had already started is correct, while the present forms do not fit the past narrative.
items.reference: Cambridge B2 First Syllabus - Vocabulary and Grammar

items.stem: Choose the correct form. If I blank you, I would apologise at once and explain what happened.
items.explanation: This second conditional uses were after If I followed by would in the main clause, so am, will be and would be break the pattern.
items.reference: Cambridge B2 First Syllabus - Vocabulary and Grammar

items.stem: Choose the correct form. This is blank book I have ever read on the subject of design.
items.explanation: The superlative with ever requires the most interesting, while the comparative forms and the plain most interesting without the do not complete the structure.
items.reference: Cambridge B2 First Syllabus - Vocabulary and Grammar

items.stem: Choose the word that best completes the sentence. He made a great blank to the success of the whole project.
items.explanation: After a great the sentence needs the noun contribution, while contribute is a verb and the other forms cannot follow the article and adjective.
items.reference: Cambridge B2 First Syllabus - Vocabulary and Grammar

items.stem: Choose the correct form of the word. The instructions were so blank that nobody in the group could follow them.
items.explanation: Instructions that cause confusion are described as confusing, whereas confused describes a person and confuse and confusion do not fit after so.
items.reference: Cambridge B2 First Syllabus - Vocabulary and Grammar

items.stem: Choose the correct modal verb. You blank have told me earlier, because I could have helped you.
items.explanation: Criticising a past omission uses should have told, while must have told states certainty and can and will cannot combine with have in this sense.
items.reference: Cambridge B2 First Syllabus - Vocabulary and Grammar

items.stem: Choose the correct form for reported speech. She said that she blank the report the day before and had sent it by email.
items.explanation: Reported speech shifts a past action to the past perfect, so had finished is correct, while the present and future forms do not match the day before.
items.reference: Cambridge B2 First Syllabus - Vocabulary and Grammar

items.stem: Choose the correct form. I look forward to blank from you soon about the interview.
items.explanation: The expression look forward to is followed by a gerund, so hearing is correct, while hear, heard and be hearing do not follow this pattern.
items.reference: Cambridge B2 First Syllabus - Vocabulary and Grammar

items.stem: Choose the correct article. He is blank honest man who never tells lies to anyone.
items.explanation: The word honest begins with a vowel sound, so the indefinite article an is used, whereas a would precede a consonant sound.
items.reference: Cambridge B2 First Syllabus - Vocabulary and Grammar

items.stem: Choose the correct relative word. That is the house blank roof was badly damaged in the storm.
items.explanation: Possession for a thing is shown with whose, so whose roof is correct, while who refers to people and which and that cannot show possession here.
items.reference: Cambridge B2 First Syllabus - Vocabulary and Grammar

items.stem: Choose the correct preposition to complete the sentence. I am not familiar blank this software and need some training.
items.explanation: The adjective familiar takes the preposition with when describing knowledge of something, while to, of and for do not form this collocation.
items.reference: Cambridge B2 First Syllabus - Vocabulary and Grammar

items.stem: Choose the best phrasal verb. The car broke blank on the motorway, so we called for help.
items.explanation: To break down means to stop working, which fits the need to call for help, while break up, break out and break in have different meanings.
items.reference: Cambridge B2 First Syllabus - Vocabulary and Grammar

items.stem: Choose the correct form of the word. Her blank was obvious from the way she smiled at everyone in the room.
items.explanation: The possessive her requires a noun, so happiness is correct, while happy is an adjective and happily and happiest are other forms.
items.reference: Cambridge B2 First Syllabus - Vocabulary and Grammar

items.stem: Choose the best linking word. He studied hard every evening, and blank, he passed the exam easily.
items.explanation: Passing easily is a consequence of studying hard, so as a result fits, while however, although and in contrast signal a different or opposing idea.
items.reference: Cambridge B2 First Syllabus - Vocabulary and Grammar

items.stem: Choose the phrase that best completes the sentence. After all her revision, the exam was a piece of blank.
items.explanation: The fixed idiom a piece of cake means something very easy, so cake is correct, while bread, pie and fruit do not form this idiom.
items.reference: Cambridge B2 First Syllabus - Vocabulary and Grammar

items.stem: Choose the correct verb form. She blank in London since 2015 and still works at the same hospital.
items.explanation: With since and a situation continuing to the present, the present perfect has lived is correct, while the other forms do not express that ongoing period.
items.reference: Cambridge B2 First Syllabus - Vocabulary and Grammar

items.stem: Choose the correct form. There is not blank milk left in the fridge, so we need to buy more.
items.explanation: Milk is uncountable, so much is used in the negative, while many, few and a few are used with countable nouns.
items.reference: Cambridge B2 First Syllabus - Vocabulary and Grammar

items.stem: Choose the correct word. The film was blank good that I watched it twice in the same week.
items.explanation: The structure so plus adjective plus that expresses result, so so good that is correct, while such needs a noun and too and very do not fit this pattern.
items.reference: Cambridge B2 First Syllabus - Vocabulary and Grammar
